What are you recording?

A 25 / 50 / 100 h, interim or 6-month check records its own fields. An annual adds optional steps (hours, workpack, CRS, ARC / permit). An extension adjusts the hours or the date to the next check. An extension is added on top of the last check — it never replaces it. Give the hours granted, the date it runs until, or both. The annual records its own date and time; the hours, workpack, CRS and ARC / permit are optional steps below — open the ones that apply.
The day the aircraft was released to service. Not in the future.
Defaults to now. Flights before this time count to the previous check, flights after it to this one.
Flying hours allowed from this check until the next one ({{ vm.hoursPlaceholder() }}). Never pre-filled with the current figure.
{{ vm.nextCheckHint() }}. Valid up to 23:59 on that day.
Shown on the fleet list so managers can plan the downtime (a 50 h check ≈ half a day, a 100 h check ≈ 2 days).
The engineer who signed the aircraft off.
Defaults to now.
Added to the hours remaining (normally up to 5 h). Leave blank for a date-only extension.
The new date of the next check. Leave blank for an hours-only extension.
